chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Musa ibn Ibrahim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the sale of pasture (kal'a) and meadows, so he said: There is no problem with it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had reserved Al-Naqi' for the cavalry horses of the Muslims.

key_terms.النَّقِيعَ: Al-Naqi', a specific place known for its pasture
key_terms.الْكَلَإِ: Pasture or grazing land, often implying enclosed or designated grazing areas
key_terms.لِخَيْلِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: For the cavalry horses of the Muslims

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell pasture land in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of selling pasture lands (kal'a) by citing the Prophet’s reservation of Al-Naqi' for the Muslim cavalry, demonstrating that public grazing lands could be designated for specific communal or military utility. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a key precedent for the concept of 'hima' (protected zones) and the state's authority to manage and transfer rights over natural resources for the public good.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Musa Bin Ibrahim, 
from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about selling the pasture, and the meadow, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it. Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had reserved Al Naqie (name of a place) for the Muslim cavalry horses’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ‘Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan from Musa ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about selling grass and pastures.

He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful, the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, had reserved al-Naqi‘ (name of a place) for the horses of the Muslims.’”
